prior_importants.description: tsc now writes straight into the repo-root ./.pup-build.XXXXXX stage. Its output sits at .pup-build.X/cli/index.js and similar, which no .gitignore rule matches: the `dist/` rule only covered the previous head's .pup-build.X/dist/ layout. While the stage holds output, git status in a worktree lists about 330 untracked .js and .js.map files (about 165 non-test modules, two files each). Two checks in pup read that status. The merge gate's worktree-clean stage (merge-gate.service.ts:2329-2343) fails with 'Uncommitted changes'. The generated Bash scope re-check (profile-compiler.service.ts:1047-1061, cap RECHECK_MAX_DIRTY_PATHS=200) fails with 'over 200 dirty paths... every Bash call is refused'. Below the cap it reports SCOPE VIOLATIONs and blames the wrong command. Triggers: (a) a parallel or background Bash call whose PostToolUse check runs between tsc's emit and the swap. That window can last up to 10s while a second build in the same worktree waits for the lock. (b) A build SIGKILLed after the emit, which leaves the stage behind for good. From then on every Bash call in the session is refused and the gate refuses the branch until someone deletes it by hand. On the previous head both cases were invisible to git.

findings.description: `rm -f dist/.gitignore` has no WHY. The root `.gitignore` already ignores `dist/`, so a reader sees a file that is created at line 17, moved into place, then deleted, and can't tell whether the delete matters. Add a one-line reason, or drop the line if nothing depends on it.
